newsitem.title: USA: Georgia's County Commissioners outline priorities.
newsitem.headline: Georgia's County Commissioners outline priorities.

text.p: County officials in Georgia endorsed a proposed gasoline tax hike Monday and called for increased accountability by public hospital authorities.
The Association of County Commissioners, which represents the state's 159 county governments, released its recommendations as the General Assembly convened Monday for its annual session.

The group said it backed a proposal by the Georgia Department of Transportation Task Force to raise the gasoline tax to 15.5 cents a gallon, from 7.5 cents a gallon, to finance highway improvements. It described the increase as "modest."
"Georgia's motor fuel tax remains the nation's lowest and, counties maintain, inadequate," the association said.
The tax increase would have to be adopted by Constitutional amendment, which requires a statewide referendum, association Executive Director Jerry Griffin said.
Gov. Zell Miller, who vetoed a 5-cents-a-gallon gasoline tax increase last year, has vowed to veto any increase again this year.
The county group also said it would support any proposal to increase public accountability by hospital authorities as they enter into management agreements with controlled corporations.

"It is absolutely vital that communities have a say in the operation of their local hospitals, what services they will provide, and how and by whom they are managed," association President Glenda Battle said.
Counties support welfare reforms but hope to minimize the impact on local property taxpayers, in anticipation of higher demands to serve the poor, Griffin said.

"Counties will promote the repeal or amendment of law requiring that hospital authority sale or lease proceeds be placed in a local trust fund, to be used only for in-hospital indigent care," he said.
